wall_kit.corners: none specified: borrow dressed-stone (FAMILY_FALLBACK crypt-stone -> dressed-stone), as log-cabin borrows rough-timber
wall_kit.rule: special panels REPLACE a plain wall-straight panel on a wall edge (they are 'kit edge' pieces 18-24 in thick: keep their room face flush with the plain wall's room face and let the extra thickness go outward); never on an edge that has a door, never used for an exterior corner

rooms.label: Antechamber
rooms.reads_as: the mourning statue (or draped-urn monument) centred on the far wall, a brazier each side of it, stone benches along the side walls; the way in is the iron gate

program.why: one axial focal piece opposite the main door, flanked symmetrically (ROOMS.md principle 8); the rest hugs the walls and the middle stays clear as a through-way
program.focal_rule: focal piece centred on the wall opposite the main door, facing it; if that wall has the onward door, put the focal in the centre of the room instead and let the path pass either side
program.flank: 2 x brazier-standing (or brazier-tripod, rite-sacred-flame-bowl), one each side of the focal, 3-4 ft off it
program.walls: bench-stone along each side wall (1 per 10 ft of wall, max 4); urn-decorative in the two corners of the door wall; pedestal-display only in rooms of 20 cells or more
program.centre: empty (walking line door -> focal -> onward door)
program.doors: main door = crypt-gate-iron in wall-doorway--crypt-stone; other doors = door-crypt; one blind wall panel may be swapped for tomb-door-sealed--crypt-stone (a style roll, 1 in 3)
program.hung: rite-memorial-plaque (2-4, at 54 in, spaced along the side walls above the benches), burial-urn-niche (0-2, mount 36 in), rite-death-mask (0-1)

counts.12 cells: 1 focal, 2 braziers, 2 benches, 2 urns, 2 plaques, 2 wall torches
counts.24 cells: 1 focal, 2 braziers, 4 benches, 4 urns, 1 pedestal, 4 plaques, 2 urn niches, 4 wall torches, 2 pillars

lights.torch: torch-sconce / torch-bracket-rough on the walls, one every 10-12 ft, alternating sides; never on a niche or ossuary panel
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light
lights.candle: candle-drippings-mound at the focal's foot (1 in 2)

rooms.label: Burial vault
rooms.reads_as: sarcophagi in the middle of the floor (one centred, or rows of them), burial-niche wall panels along the long walls, tall candle stands at the tomb's corners

program.why: small: one tomb promoted to the centre like the fine-room bed; from about 25 cells it becomes an aisle room (store / dormitory grammar) with 'sarcophagus' as the row item
program.focal_rule: under 20 cells: ONE sarcophagus in the centre, long axis along the room's long axis, foot toward the main door. 20 cells and up: rows of sarcophagi, long axis across the room, 4 ft aisles, a 5 ft cross aisle at the door end; mix skus s1/s2/s3 so neighbours differ; the far-end centre tomb is effigy-knight when present (the 'founder')
program.open_state: about 1 tomb in 6 is placed OPEN (sarcophagus-open--s1 or --s1--lidoff), never the founder; only sarcophagus--s1 has a matching twin, so an open tomb is always the s1 design
program.walls: long walls: swap 1 in 2 plain wall panels for wall-crypt-niches--crypt-stone (s1 empty / s2 wrapped bodies / s3 bones, rolled per panel, never on a door edge and never both sides of a corner). Against the remaining plain wall: coffin (0-3, some stacked two high is NOT supported: single only), stone-coffin-lidless (0-1), bench-stone (0-1), urn-decorative in corners
program.centre: the tombs; tomb-slab (mesh) or decal-grave-ledger (flat) in the floor of the cross aisle, 0-2
program.on_things: rite-canopic-jars-set at the foot of 1 tomb in 4 (on the floor beside it); skull-single / candle-drippings-mound on a closed lid, 1 in 5
program.hung: rite-memorial-plaque on plain panels (1 per 15 ft), rite-death-mask (0-1), burial-urn-niche (0-2)

counts.20 cells: 1-2 sarcophagi, 4 niche panels, 2 coffins, 4 candle stands, 2 wall torches, 2 urns
counts.40 cells: 6 sarcophagi (1 open, 1 effigy), 8 niche panels, 3 coffins, 6 candle stands, 4 wall torches, 2 pillars, 2 ledgers

lights.torch: torch-sconce / torch-bracket-rough on the walls, one every 10-12 ft, alternating sides; never on a niche or ossuary panel
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light
lights.candle: rite-pillar-candle-tall (or candlestand-pricket / candle-tree / candlestick-floor) at the head corners of the focal tomb: 2 for one tomb, 2 per row end in an aisle room

program.density: floor coverage 25-30% by tombs in an aisle vault

rooms.label: Ossuary
rooms.reads_as: the bone shrine on the far wall, walls faced with skulls (ossuary-wall panels), a skull-faced pillar or two and bone troughs along the sides

program.why: a storeroom of bones: the walls carry the stock, the floor carries heaps and troughs, one axial focal on the far wall
program.focal_rule: ossuary-shrine centred on the wall opposite the door (a 'wall' piece, flat back to the wall); if absent, a large skull-pile in the centre
program.walls: swap 2 in 3 plain panels for ossuary-wall--crypt-stone (s2, the arched-niche one, at most once per wall); the panel behind the shrine stays plain. catacomb-shelf-bones (s1/s2) against the remaining plain panels, 1-3; charnel-trough along a side wall, 1 per 15 ft
program.centre: ossuary-pillar where a support would go (2 from 16 cells, 4 from 30, on a grid, never in the door-shrine line); skull-pile and bones-pile in the corners and at pillar feet (like with like: heaps cluster), 2-5
program.scatter: decal-bones-scatter thinly over the floor (flat), never on the door-shrine path

counts.16 cells: 1 shrine, 5 ossuary panels, 2 pillars, 1 trough, 1 shelf, 3 heaps, 2 lights
counts.30 cells: 1 shrine, 9 ossuary panels, 4 pillars, 2 troughs, 3 shelves, 5 heaps, 4 lights

lights.candle: candle-drippings-mound either side of the shrine; skull-candle on troughs and shelves' tops (surface, 1-3); rite-bone-candelabra on the shrine's altar top (surface, 0-1); rite-pillar-candle-tall flanking the shrine in big rooms
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light

rooms.label: Catacomb corridor
rooms.reads_as: both long walls lined with burial-niche panels, wall torches between them, the odd coffin or bone heap pushed against a wall

program.why: door -> door walking line down the middle, everything else alternates along the long sides
program.focal_rule: the key feature is the WALLS: on both long sides swap 2 in 3 plain panels for wall-crypt-niches--crypt-stone (s1/s2/s3 rolled per panel; runs of 2-3 niche panels, then one plain panel that carries the torch)
program.walls: against plain panels only, alternating sides to slow the run: catacomb-shelf-bones (1 per 25 ft), coffin on the floor along the wall (0-2), stone-coffin-lidless (0-1), rite-mummified-remains on the floor along the wall (0-1)
program.centre: clear 3 ft walking line; skull-pile / bones-pile only in end corners and dead ends (1-3)
program.scatter: decal-bones-scatter and decal-moss, thin; decal-cobweb in top corners and across unused doorways
program.hung: burial-urn-niche on plain panels (0-2); rite-memorial-plaque beside a niche run (0-2)

counts.12 cells (30 ft): 8 niche panels of 12 long-wall panels, 2-3 wall torches, 1 shelf, 1 coffin, 1 heap
counts.24 cells (60 ft): 16 niche panels, 5 wall torches, 2 shelves, 2 coffins, 1 lidless coffin, 2 heaps

lights.torch: torch-sconce / torch-bracket-rough (or lantern-wall-iron) on the plain panels between niche runs, alternating sides, one every 12-15 ft: darker than other rooms on purpose
lights.candle: candle-drippings-mound on the floor under one niche panel (0-2)
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light

program.density: about 3 props per 100 sq ft plus the wall panels

rooms.label: Chapel of rest
rooms.reads_as: the altar on the far short wall, a pall-draped coffin on its bier lying in the middle before it with a tall candle at each corner, rows of stone benches facing the altar

program.why: no existing program is a chapel; it is an axial focal (the altar, as the hearth on a short wall) plus the aisle grammar with benches as the row item, all facing the focal. A new small 'chapel' program is the honest fit and the castle chapel can share it
program.focal_rule: altar-stone centred on the SHORT wall opposite the door, 1.5 ft off the wall. rite-funeral-pall (or the empty rite-funeral-bier, 1 in 4) on the centre line 5-6 ft in front of the altar, long axis on the room's axis: this is the second key feature and is dropped only under 15 cells
program.rows: bench-stone (s1/s2; pew when its mesh exists) in two blocks either side of a 4 ft centre aisle, facing the altar, rows 3.5 ft apart, starting 4 ft behind the bier and stopping 4 ft short of the door wall; 1 bench per side per row
program.flank: statue-weeping-angel or monument-urn-draped in ONE corner beside the altar (0-1); urn-decorative pair on the altar wall corners; lectern beside the altar on the door-side left when its mesh exists
program.on_things: on the altar: rite-altar-cloth (flat) under candelabra x2 at the ends + one of rite-offering-candles-tray / reliquary / tome-holy in the middle; vase-flowers or flowers-dried at the bier's foot
program.ceiling: censer-hanging over the bier or rite-sanctuary-lamp over the altar front (one of each at most)
program.hung: rite-memorial-plaque along the side walls (2-4); sconce-candle-single between them

counts.20 cells: 1 altar, 1 pall/bier, 4 corner candles, 4-6 benches, 1 statue, 1 hanging lamp, 2 plaques, 2 altar candelabra
counts.36 cells: 1 altar, 1 pall/bier, 4 corner candles, 10 benches, 1 statue, 2 urns, 1 sand tray, censer + lamp, 4 plaques, 4 wall sconces

lights.candle: rite-pillar-candle-tall (or candlestand-pricket / candle-tree / candlestick-floor) at the FOUR corners of the bier; candelabra on the altar; rite-memorial-sand-tray against a side wall near the door (from 24 cells); sconce-candle-single on side walls
lights.torch: torch-sconce only on the door wall
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light; the brightest crypt room, candle-lit

rooms.label: Embalming room
rooms.reads_as: the stone table in the middle of the room (empty or with a shrouded body), a salt tub beside it, shelves of jars on one wall and coffins waiting against another

program.why: a work room: a central work table with standing room all round, a work line of shelves and a prep table on the walls, storage in the corners
program.focal_rule: the slab in the centre, long axis along the room's long axis, 3 ft clear on all four sides; rite-corpse-on-slab 2 times in 3, the empty embalming-table otherwise. From 24 cells: a second slab parallel to the first, 5 ft apart, one empty and one occupied
program.companions: natron-tub within reach of the slab's foot end (the drain spout end); bucket or bucket-slop under the spout; linen-wrappings-basket by the head end
program.walls: one wall = the work line: table-kitchen-prep (carrying rite-embalming-tools, rite-canopic-jars-set, candlestick) + shelving-freestanding x1-2 (jars: rite-canopic-jar, jar-lidded-stoneware, storage-jar, oil-jar; rite-burial-shroud-folded). Opposite wall: coffin x1-2 on the floor, coffin-maker-stack in a corner (from 16 cells), rite-mummified-remains on the floor by the door = finished work (0-1). washstand or basin-stone on the door wall
program.ceiling: lantern-hanging over the slab; censer-hanging in a corner (0-1)
program.hung: shelf-wall above the prep table; rite-death-mask (0-2) on the wall

counts.12 cells: 1 slab, 1 tub, 1 prep table, 1 shelving, 1 coffin, 1 bucket, 1 basket, 6 jars, 2 lights
counts.24 cells: 2 slabs, 1 tub, 2 prep tables, 2 shelving, 2 coffins + stack, washstand, 12 jars, 4 lights

lights.lantern: lantern-hanging over the slab (ceiling), lantern-wall-iron on the work-line wall
lights.candle: candlestick / candle on the prep table
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light

rooms.label: Relic chamber
rooms.reads_as: the gold reliquary shrine in the centre (or on the far wall) with a fire bowl each side, treasure against the walls: an open chest of gold, coin heaps, grave goods, urns

program.why: one axial focal (as the front-desk counter) with a symmetric pair of lights; treasure is edge fill like a storeroom's
program.focal_rule: reliquary-shrine centred opposite the door, 2 ft off the far wall (in rooms of 16 cells and up: dead centre). Without it: pedestal-display in the centre carrying reliquary / casket-ornate / reliquary-hand
program.flank: rite-sacred-flame-bowl x2 (or brazier-standing / brazier-tripod), one each side of the focal
program.walls: chest-treasure in a far corner angled 15-30 degrees toward the door (the reward shot); chest-ironbound / chest-plain along the side walls (1-3); coin-pile and rite-grave-goods-pile beside the chests (like with like); urn-decorative pair on the door wall; pedestal-display x2 on the side walls carrying reliquary-hand, rite-relic-bone-fragment, casket-ornate, urn-ashes-small (from 12 cells); monument-urn-draped in a corner (from 20 cells)
program.doors: exactly one door: door-crypt (shut) or crypt-gate-iron (you can see the gold through the bars); a tomb-door-sealed--crypt-stone panel may stand in for a second door
program.hung: rite-death-mask (1-2) on the far wall either side of the shrine

counts.9 cells: 1 shrine, 2 fire bowls, 1 treasure chest, 1 coin pile, 1 chest, 2 urns
counts.20 cells: 1 shrine, 2 fire bowls, 1 treasure chest, 2 coin piles, 1 grave goods, 3 chests, 2 pedestals with relics, 2 urns, 1 monument, 2 masks

lights.brazier: rite-sacred-flame-bowl / brazier-standing / brazier-tripod flanking the focal
lights.torch: torch-sconce on the door wall only
lights.note: no windows anywhere: every crypt room must get at least one light
